dedupe_keys.name: inundation2depth carolina urban flood extent and derived depth tiles

description: Inundation2Depth pairs flood extent and depth labels with terrain and land-surface features across twelve flood-affected areas in North and South Carolina. Researchers combined aerial imagery, LiDAR digital terrain models and hydrostatic water-surface assumptions, then packaged raw and normalized scene-level data and 5,925 overlapping image tiles. The public Zenodo release provides two ZIP archives under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is selected historical events and urban places, not all Carolina roads or a real-time flood-depth feed. Depth labels are derived from terrain and inundation assumptions, not direct depth observations at every pixel. The article describes hydrodynamic comparison using HEC-RAS; it does not eliminate uncertainty in labels or ground elevations. A reviewer-assessed use is testing urban flood-depth mapping or road-access exposure methods. data-fema-national-flood-hazard-layer is a related US flood reference, not the source of these event tiles. The article’s preview URL included a token-like parameter; this review used the untokened public record. No archive was downloaded. Simulation users should treat the derived depths as conditional labels.
